scope: out-of-band pairing: pairing card transfer, explicit trust confirmation, SAS P-256 fix

fix.problem: the previous round stored an empty P-256 fingerprint for code-based (Rust SAS) pairings, so those pairings refused to sync
fix.cause: the Android side passes DeviceIdentity.fingerprint() (P-256) into nativePairDial/nativePairServe, and the Rust SAS binds both fingerprints plus both transport keys, so the peer P-256 fingerprint was available all along
fix.change: code-based pairing now records remoteFingerprint as the P-256 identity; both pairing paths are channel-bound

out_of_band.card: TRACEWEAVE-PAIRING-CARD-1 text block with fingerprint, peerId, optional multiaddr and an 8-hex checksum; copy/paste through the system clipboard so the user carries it between devices
out_of_band.confirmation: the manual path no longer derives a display-only 6-digit code; it shows an explicit 'trust this fingerprint?' dialog that states the fingerprint is only safe if the user carried it out of band
out_of_band.removed: SyncPairing.pairingNonce/code (they were a typo aid presented next to a fingerprint field, not an authentication step); the fingerprint path now uses SyncPairing.pairOutOfBand

verification.host_tests: 95 pass, including test_pairing_card (round-trip, optional address, bad magic, checksum, uppercase fingerprint, invalid peer id/address, malformed/unknown field, truncated card)
verification.device: 0.1.5 installed; pairing dialog shows the card buttons; copying then pasting filled the remote fields; the OOB confirmation dialog rendered with the warning; cancelling left 0 paired devices; RUN_SUITE 48 / TASK_CENTER 10 / RUN_DOCUMENTS 20 PASS
verification.not_verified: an actual two-device card exchange and code-based pairing still need the second phone

known_gaps: the pairing card trusts the channel the user carries it through; clipboard leaks (e.g. clipboard history apps) are outside the app's control
no QR code or camera scanning; transfer is clipboard/manual
the Rust SAS exchange still runs over LAN discovery, which needs multicast to work on the shared network
